body:
- Buying during pessimism: Titan was "a poorly performing stock" in 2002-03 when he bought it. — [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/indias-warren-buffett-the-man-with-the-midas-touch-who-was-rakesh-jhunjhunwala/1082239). He held through volatility because there was "no permanent impairment of value". — [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/interview/you-cant-make-money-on-borrowed-knowledge-566)
- Paying up for quality: Damani's "Peddar Road at Dharavi's rates" line on HDFC Bank. — [Rediff](https://www.rediff.com/business/special/how-well-do-you-know-d-marts-damani/20170405.htm)
- Both made big money on the bear side in 1992. — [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/indias-warren-buffett-the-man-with-the-midas-touch-who-was-rakesh-jhunjhunwala/1082239); [Rediff](https://www.rediff.com/business/special/how-well-do-you-know-d-marts-damani/20170405.htm)
- Concentration: Titan was about one-third of Jhunjhunwala's portfolio. — [BNN Bloomberg](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/indian-billionaire-s-stock-holdings-worth-nearly-4-billion-in-focus-after-death-1.1806140.amp.html). Damani's 82% D-Mart stake was about 90% of his net worth at IPO (₹32,000 crore of more than ₹35,000 crore). — [Rediff](https://www.rediff.com/business/special/how-well-do-you-know-d-marts-damani/20170405.htm)
- Mistakes from misjudging promoters (A2Z, Bilcare). — [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/interview/you-cant-make-money-on-borrowed-knowledge-566)

body:
`insight:capital-light-compounding` · confidence: verified

Cases: Monster (outsourced bottling + distributors; best US stock of 30 years, ~+200,000%), Costco (membership fees ~ most of profit; ~29x since 2009), Constellation Software (~300x via small VMS acquisitions funded by FCF), Domino's (franchise; ~180x from trough), Hermès (scarcity pricing; ~30x), Booking (agency model). Shared traits: high returns on incremental capital, someone else funds the assets (co-packers, franchisees, suppliers via negative working capital, customers via membership fees), long-tenured owner-managers (Sacks/Schlosberg, Munger's influence, Leonard, Dumas family), and EPS growth doing most of the work for a decade or more. Early signals: rising gross margin with flat capex, renewal/retention data, management letters reporting ROIC honestly. Where they stall: (1) key-person exit plus a new threat (Constellation -51% after Leonard left + AI fears); (2) the multiple gets ahead of growth (Costco ~50-60x on high-single-digit growth; Hermès ~50x before a ~-50% fall); (3) growth slows to GDP-plus (Monster 2022-24, Domino's 2022-26). Lesson: these are the best 'hold forever' candidates, but late-stage returns depend on entry multiple; a P/E doubling in the last stretch is a non-repeatable gift.

- **Links:** `case_study:monster-beverage-2002-2024`, `case_study:costco-2009-2026`, `case_study:constellation-software-2006-2026`, `insight:twin-engine`, `strategy:marcellus-cc`
